subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the call [Thinking]
passage: The call with the alumnus was at 5 p.m. and Varun had been pacing his room since lunch. His flatmate Chinmay watched him mutter. "Are you talking to yourself?" "Practising." Varun had a note card: opening line, "Thank you for making time; I read your article on delivery planning." Then two questions: "How did you pick your first project?" and "What would you do differently?" He also imagined the worst: a long silence on the line. What would he say? He decided: "Take your time, I have another question ready." Seeing it coming made silence feel like a pause, not a disaster. At 4:55 his hands were cold, but not shaking. When the call started, he said the first line as planned.

qa.q: What time was Varun's call with the alumnus?
What is Varun feeling as the call approaches?
qa.a: Varun feels nervous, with cold hands, but steadier than before because he has rehearsed for the awkward moments.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Varun add, and why?
qa.a: Varun could do a mock call with Chinmay asking surprising questions, because rehearsing alone cannot reproduce a real person's unexpected turns.

qa.q: How does Chinmay see Varun's practice?
qa.a: Chinmay watches Varun mutter and asks if he is talking to himself, so Chinmay may find it odd at first but learns it is a plan.

'Okay, Kamal, you're the engineer. Pretend.' Tarun sat on the hostel bed, phone face down.
'Fine. Hello?'
'Hi, thanks for taking the time. I'm Tarun, I wrote about your talk on water sensors.' He stopped. 'Too fast?'
'Bit fast. Again.'
Tarun said it again, slower. 'Then question one: how did you test the sensors in the field? Question two: what would you tell a student starting in this area?'
'And if I just say "hmm" and go quiet?'
Tarun's hands went cold even though it was pretend. 'Then... I wait three seconds. Then I say, "Maybe I can ask it differently," and go to question two.'
'Good. Your voice is shaking.'
'I know. That's fine. It'll shake at five o'clock too. At least I know what comes after it.'
At five, the real call began, and his voice shook for the first line only.

qa.a: What would you tell a student starting in this area?

qa.q: How did Tarun feel when Kamal imagined the call going quiet, and what shows it?
qa.a: Tarun felt nervous; his hands went cold even though it was pretend, but planning the next step made the fear more manageable.

qa.q: What else could Tarun rehearse before the next call?
qa.a: How to close the call politely and ask whether it is fine to stay in touch, so the ending feels as prepared as the start.

qa.q: What is the rehearsal like for Kamal?
qa.a: Kamal plays the engineer and gets to test Tarun gently, noticing the shaking voice without making fun of it.

grounding: Shows a student rehearsing the opening line, two questions and a silent pause before a call, so the real nerves feel manageable.

subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the call [Thinking]
passage:
I'm Thomas, and before my first call with a stranger I did something that felt silly: I rehearsed it on a walk around the hostel football ground.
The stranger was Naveen, an engineer at a solar firm who had agreed to fifteen minutes. On my first lap I said my opening line out loud: 'Thanks for making time, I'm the student who asked about panel cleaning.' On the second lap I practised my two questions.
On the third lap I did the part I was dreading. I imagined Naveen going silent after my first question and let the silence sit in my head for a few steps. My stomach dropped. Then I told myself: silence means thinking, not boredom. Wait, then ask the second one.
When the call came, Naveen did go quiet after my first question. I felt the same drop, recognised it, and waited. The answer, when it came, took eight minutes.

qa.q: Where did Thomas rehearse the call?
qa.a: On a walk around the hostel football ground.

qa.q: What did Thomas feel when Naveen really went quiet, and why was it easier then?
qa.a: Thomas felt the same drop in the stomach but stayed calm, because that silence had already been imagined and a plan was ready.

qa.q: Which other approach could help Thomas before an even bigger call?
qa.a: Practising with a friend who plays the other person, since a real voice can surprise in ways a solo walk cannot.

qa.q: How might the call have felt for Naveen?
qa.a: Naveen could think for a moment without being rushed, so the answer came out full and useful and took eight minutes.

grounding: Shows a student rehearsing an opening line, two questions and an imagined silence, so the real call's nerves feel less threatening.
